title: Comparative study regarding the efficiency of different technologies for the intraoperative elimination of surgical smoke during body contouring surgery
summary: This study investigates the two main technologies for eliminating surgical smoke during electrosurgery. These devices have been approved for many years and are used in operating rooms worldwide. Participating patients are randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group uses conventional smoke extraction, where the smoke is drawn away from the instruments. The other group uses electroprecipitation, which uses an electric current to deposit the smoke gases on the body, preventing the smoke from entering the surrounding air. We aim to determine which technique is most effective. Direct comparative data is currently lacking. It is evident that each manufacturer markets its own technology/product as the best method. Our study will rigorously examine this scientifically. The two different systems will be compared.

interventions.name: The aim of this study is to transfer and verify the findings obtained from ex vivo, in vivo, and routine clinical practice to open electrosurgery. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients over 18 years of age for whom body contouring surgery is indicated due to massive weight loss. Patients scheduled for breast/thorax lift, abdominoplasty (also known as fleur-de-lis lift) will be included.

Consent to study participation
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent to study participation. Otherwise, there are no preoperative exclusion criteria.
